# Discussion

**Main finding.** In autoregressive generation, behavioral intervention
magnitude can be created at a causal handoff from graded latent state
to a discrete emitted token. Crossing the decoding boundary exposes a
high-gain public continuation channel, so a large free-generation effect
need not imply a comparably large persistent latent effect. For the
attribution-selected S1 intervention at \(5\times\), treated-article
replay reproduces the new top noun on 20/20 prompts;
\(\operatorname{cosine}(E_M,E_T)=0.95\), while matched-prefix leftover TV
is \(0.028\) and comparable to a random control. Between two gains
separated by at most \(0.0039\) that bracket the article argmax, fixed-article
distributions move only \(0.014\) TV while the free-path noun distribution
jumps \(0.938\) TV in near-perfect token-substitution alignment.

This is a **transmission** result, not evidence that no latent plan exists.
Representation at \(P\) and transmission of its later effect are distinct;
the assay separates generated-token relay from matched-prefix leftover, not
fused packages from modular plans. The six-cell assay tells us which
channel carries the intervention. The boundary experiment tells us why its
behavioral magnitude can become enormous.

The precision and temperature audits refine that conclusion. The coarse
native boundary margins reflect bfloat16 readout quantization, not a
discrete internal state. Yet a float32 head preserves the sharp
cross-boundary continuation change, and stochastic policies preserve a
graded version whose magnitude follows article-policy movement. The
relevant mechanism is therefore decoder gain: graded latent evidence
controls a public symbolic action whose reuse at the next step strongly
reshapes the continuation distribution.

**Replay as a falsifier.** If the article carries the later change, replaying
it in an unintervened run should recreate that change [@chan2022scrubbing].
It does; \(E_T=E_M+E_R\) makes this an exact vector split.

**Separately intervenable routes.** In this model and task, visible token
identity and contextual information propagated from the previous position
are separately intervenable causes of noun prediction. The public token
behaves as a low-bandwidth discrete relay for coarse class information,
while a target-constructed residual patch shows that a private contextual
channel can carry finer target-specific information. These are not two
independent registers: the observed
interaction shows that the effects are not additive, the patch is applied
at \(P\) rather than under the article token, and the two factors do not
necessarily carry the same information.

Natural target-state patches strengthen the private half of this picture:
they enhance target logits, partly suppress source logits, reverse sign
when the direction is reversed, and exceed wrong-target and Gaussian
controls without explicit noun cues. But neither same- nor cross-class
prompts convert that state into an article change because those targets are
different meanings and the interventions are subthreshold.

The correctness-preserving synonym assay supplies the missing controlled
comparison. It holds semantic acceptability constant, uses one residual-patch
construction, and changes whether the article can encode the distinction
between two lexical realizations. Cross-article alternatives become
public-relay dominant; within-article alternatives retain their intended
lexical movement in the private component. In mediator-relative terms, article
identity distinguishes the former outcomes but places the latter in one
equivalence class. The signed target projection shows both simple effects
independently, yielding a causal double dissociation; unsigned TV supports the
interaction but not an independent within-class simple effect. The result
demonstrates route recruitment in a constructed lexical-choice task, not a
claim that natural prompts dynamically choose a carrier, that a sparse mechanism
performs the allocation, or that information is moved wholesale from private to
public storage.

**A closed-loop gain composition replaces a channel-label interpretation.** Article
attribution has held-out validity for local margin movement, directionally at
both scales. Matched signed future-target analyses remain inconclusive rather
than demonstrating independence. Public influence is nevertheless predictable:
it is exactly policy movement times the fixed-branch continuation leverage.
Attribution estimates one input to that composition; baseline decoder
susceptibility and branch leverage supply the others. The factorization itself
is the elementary algebra of a finite mixture; the empirical contribution is
measuring its factors separately and showing that the 270M composition predicts
cells holding out both feature and prompt, while simple baselines do not. Weak
transferable local calibration limits prediction at 1B. The positive principle is therefore
that local causal pressure, decoder susceptibility, and continuation leverage
are separately measurable—not that attribution categorically cannot predict a
channel.

**The causal-validity ladder.** The 1B assays show why candidate-signal evidence,
local efficacy, mediator-support validity, and transmission identification must
be tested in order. The original sparse handle is too weak; an effect-matched
coalition moves the intended contrast but exits the binary article support; and
a constrained one-feature frontier preserves that support. Although the
frontier changes the greedy article only once, its stochastic assay identifies
low-amplitude hybrid transmission that becomes public-dominant at softer
article policies. The target-uncued, natural-state-derived residual assay
establishes private influence at both scales, but normalized estimands do not
support a monotone scale effect. The earlier natural-pair strength-by-class
interaction remains suggestive and single-pair-driven, with intervals spanning
zero; it is superseded as a carrier test by the correctness-preserving synonym
design. The cross-scale lesson is thus methodological and mechanistic: climb all
four rungs before interpreting a route, and compare scales only after
normalizing the intervention and target gap.

**Closed-loop intervention logic.** The generated article is a
self-generated consequence of the upstream state. We use closed-loop
intervention logic: replay the consequence, restore its baseline value
under perturbation, and cross external feedback with private state
[@crapse2008corollary]. The article maps to a reafferent consequence and
token replay/rescue to opening that loop; the matched-token leftover is
internal influence that survives feedback control, not a localized
corollary-discharge signal.

**Methodological standard.** Multi-token causal claims should report the six
cells, exact vector split, both fixed-token leftovers, and intervention-off
token contrast; use full-sequence recomputation and target-free distances; and
validate reachability and sensitivity. Otherwise a later-token change shows
coordinated output, not identified leftover control.
